title: Photo to Route Mapper: EXIF Photos to a Route
description: Map geotagged JPEG photo locations, sorted by available EXIF or file modification time.
summary_sentence: Photo points are connected with straight lines; the result is not a recorded or road-snapped journey.
quick_answer: This tool reads supported JPEG EXIF GPS data locally, orders photos by EXIF time or file modification time, and connects points with straight lines. The route is an approximation, not the actual path travelled; map tile requests can reveal the viewed area.

use_cases.title: Rebuilding a hike you forgot to record

body.t: No watch, no app — but forty photos. Their EXIF positions rebuild the day closely enough to log it, share it and find that viewpoint again. Export it as GPX and the
Inspection photos arrive as evidence; mapped in time order they become the inspection's route and coverage proof, asset by asset.
A road trip's photos draw the trip better than memory does — the unplanned detour is right there in the pin sequence.
Expense claims, delivery runs and field reports carry photo trails. The map they draw either matches the claim or starts a conversation.

Three hours underground in a show cave: no photos, so the route leaps from the entrance to the café. The line is a join of evidence, not a recording — where photos are silent, the map says nothing, and the straight join is drawn knowing that.

A camera whose clock was an hour off still maps correctly by position, but the sequence sorts by its wrong timestamps. Fix the clock offset in your head when the route doubles back inexplicably — EXIF time is the camera's claim, not the truth.

faq: JPEGs (and most phone HEICs converted to JPEG) whose EXIF still carries GPS coordinates. The surest test: the photo's details in your gallery show a location.
Files may lack supported EXIF GPS fields or be unreadable by this parser. Check the originals and metadata.
EXIF time is used when present, otherwise file modification time. The parser treats EXIF time as local browser time without timezone correction; order may be wrong.
Accuracy varies with device, conditions and the recorded metadata. Do not treat photo pins as surveyed positions.
Does it draw the roads we drove?
No — pins joined by straight lines in time order: a photo itinerary, not a road-snapped track. Between close photos the difference is invisible; across a photo desert it is a beeline.
What GPX does the download contain?
It includes waypoints and a straight-line track. Waypoint names and valid times are included; trackpoint times and original photo metadata are not preserved.
The photos are read locally, but map tiles can reveal the viewed area to the tile provider. Exports contain coordinates, photo names and timestamps; review before sharing.
